questions.question: When are generic type arguments checked in Java?
options: At run time, by the JVM
questions.explanation: The compiler checks every generic use and then erases the type arguments, so the JVM never sees them.

questions.question: What does this print? List<String> a = new ArrayList<>(); List<Integer> b = new ArrayList<>(); System.out.println(a.getClass() == b.getClass());
questions.explanation: Type erasure removes the type arguments, so both lists are plain ArrayList objects at run time.

questions.question: Why does List<int> stock = new ArrayList<>(); fail to compile?
options: Type arguments must be reference types, so use List<Integer>
The diamond operator is not allowed here
questions.explanation: Erased type parameters become Object or a bound, and a primitive is not an object. The wrapper Integer is used instead.

questions.question: After erasure, what does T become in class Scale<T extends Number>?
questions.explanation: A bounded type parameter is erased to its first bound, which here is Number.

questions.question: A method is declared as void load(List<Number> crates). Why does load(new ArrayList<Integer>()) not compile?
options: List<Integer> is not a subtype of List<Number>
ArrayList cannot be passed as List
questions.explanation: Generics are invariant. Declare the parameter as List<? extends Number> to accept lists of any Number subtype.

questions.question: According to PECS, which parameter type fits a method that only adds Integer values into a list?
questions.explanation: The list consumes the values you write, so Consumer Super applies. It then accepts Integer, Number or Object lists.

questions.question: Inside class Crate<T>, why is the line T spare = new T(); rejected by the compiler?
options: Constructors cannot be called in generic classes
T is not known at run time because of type erasure
new is not allowed for fields
questions.explanation: T is erased, so the JVM would not know which class to create. Pass a Supplier<T> or Class<T> instead.

questions.question: What does this print? List<? extends Number> w = Arrays.asList(4, 2.5); double s = 0; for (Number n : w) s += n.doubleValue(); System.out.println(s);
questions.explanation: Reading from a ? extends Number list is allowed, and each element is used as a Number: 4.0 + 2.5 = 6.5.

questions.question: What is the main danger of using a raw type such as List instead of List<String>?
options: It is slower to add elements
The compiler stops checking types, so wrong values fail later at run time
questions.explanation: A raw List accepts any object. The hidden cast fails only when the value is read, far from the real bug.

questions.question: In static <T> T firstOf(List<T> items), what does the <T> before the return type do?
options: It declares a type parameter for this method
It makes the method return a raw type
It marks the method as synchronized
questions.explanation: A generic method declares its own type parameters before the return type, and Java infers T from the argument.
